//: Agentiva RabbitMQ topology, imported after broker start by the one-shot
`rabbitmq-topology` container (see docker-compose.yml) via the management
HTTP API -- deliberately not via rabbitmq.conf's load_definitions, which
would suppress RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER creation on a fresh broker even with
an empty "users" array here (see infrastructure/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf).
Declaring the topology here as well as in the services is deliberate. The
services declare idempotently at startup so a developer's first
`docker compose up` works unattended, but in production they run with
DeclareTopologyOnStartup=false and this file is the reviewed source of
truth — a misconfigured replica must not be able to create a queue that
nothing drains.
The retry path is per-service rather than shared: see
src/building-blocks/Agentiva.BuildingBlocks.Messaging/Configuration/EventBusTopology.cs
for why dead-lettering a shared delay queue onto the main topic exchange
would fan a single service's retry back out to every one of its peers.
The 'agentiva-work-queues' policy below bounds every service's work queue
length: an unbounded queue hides a dead consumer until the broker runs
out of disk, whereas rejecting publishes past the bound makes the
failure visible immediately. No policy is needed for the dead-letter
queues themselves -- 'never expire a parked message automatically' is
RabbitMQ's default behaviour with no TTL set, not something a policy has
to state. A RabbitMQ policy's 'definition' object is validated strictly
against known broker settings, so -- unlike this top-level document,
which RabbitMQ does not validate as strictly -- it cannot carry an
explanatory '//' key of its own; that is why the rationale for each
policy lives here instead of beside it.
